tools.name: agent_chat
tools.title: Chat with Roboflow Agent
tools.description:
Chat with the Roboflow AI agent.

Use this tool for:

- **Roboflow Q&A** — the agent has the full Roboflow
  documentation indexed (SDKs, REST API, deployment options,
  training, batch processing, Universe, blocks, pricing,
  etc.). Ask it anything about how Roboflow works.
- **Advanced workflow building** — workflows complex enough
  that direct block composition via ``workflow_blocks_*`` is
  impractical. The agent knows every block and connection
  pattern.
- **Solution planning** — pass ``mode="plan"`` and the user's
  problem; the agent uses a stronger planning model to scope
  a CV solution end-to-end before any building happens.

For straightforward workflows you can construct yourself, the
direct ``workflow_*`` tools are fine — you don't have to route
every workflow through the agent.

## Conversation flow

The agent runs a multi-step conversation. It may ask
clarifying questions, recommend a model, or (in plan mode)
produce a plan for confirmation. Pass the returned
``conversation_id`` back on follow-up calls to keep context.
Use ``agent_conversations_list`` and ``agent_conversation_get``
to find and resume past conversations.

## Long runs

Complex turns (large workflow builds/edits) can take several
minutes. When the agent does not finish quickly, this tool
returns ``{"status": "running", "run_id": ...}`` instead of
blocking. Call ``agent_chat_result`` with that ``run_id``
repeatedly until the status is no longer ``running``; the run
keeps executing server-side in the meantime. Do NOT re-send
the same message with agent_chat, that would start a second,
duplicate run.

## CRITICAL: the agent NEVER publishes workflows

Every workflow the agent creates or edits is saved as a
**draft**. The published version that callers using the
workflow by id will hit is unchanged until you explicitly
publish.

To make agent edits live, call ``agent_workflow_publish`` with
the workflow ``url`` returned in the chat response.

## Running an agent-built workflow

With a Roboflow API key, two options are available:

1. **Run the draft directly without publishing** — pass the
   ``specification`` returned in the chat response to
   ``workflow_specs_run``. Best for testing the draft, or for
   one-off runs where you don't want to disturb the
   currently-published version.
2. **Publish, then run by id** — call
   ``agent_workflow_publish(workflow_url=...)`` then
   ``workflows_run(workflow_id=..., images=...)``. Use this
   when you want the change to go live for everyone using the
   workflow by id.

OAuth connections may not list the workflow run tools. In that
case, publish with ``agent_workflow_publish`` when ready and use
the workflow's ``app_url`` to open and test it in Roboflow.

## Where to open a workflow in the Roboflow UI

Each workflow in the ``workflows`` array has an ``app_url``
field with the canonical, environment-aware Roboflow UI URL.
``app_url`` is the authoritative link for a workflow; URLs
embedded in the agent's ``text`` reply may not match the
current environment.

## Response shape

When the run finishes within the inline wait:

- ``status`` — ``"completed"``.
- ``text`` — the agent's reply.
- ``workflows`` — workflows created or edited in this turn,
  each with ``id``, ``name``, ``url`` (slug), ``app_url``
  (clickable Roboflow UI URL — use this), and
  ``specification`` (the full draft JSON; pass it to
  the API-key-only workflow run tools to execute without
  publishing).
- ``conversation_id`` — pass back to continue the conversation.

When the run is still going: ``status`` is ``"running"`` and
``run_id`` is the handle to pass to ``agent_chat_result``.

message.description: Message for the agent (a Roboflow question, a description of an advanced workflow to build, or a request to plan a CV solution).

conversation_id.description: Conversation ID to continue a previous agent chat. Omit to start a new conversation.

mode.description: Use 'plan' to plan a CV solution end-to-end before building (uses a stronger planning model). Use 'agent' (default) for Roboflow Q&A and advanced workflow construction.

tools.name: agent_chat_result
tools.title: Get Agent Chat Result
tools.description:
Collect the result of an agent_chat run that was still working.

Waits briefly for the run to finish, then returns either the
completed chat response (same shape as ``agent_chat``) or
``{"status": "running", "run_id": ...}``. Keep calling with the
same ``run_id`` until the status is no longer ``running``. The
run keeps executing server-side between calls; polling never
restarts or duplicates it.

A ``"severed"`` status means the connection to the run was cut
mid-flight; the run usually still finishes server-side, so read
the reply from the conversation (``agent_conversation_get``)
instead of re-sending the message.

run_id.description: Run ID returned by agent_chat when the agent was still working.

tools.name: agent_conversations_list
tools.title: List Agent Conversations
tools.description:
List Roboflow agent conversations in the workspace.

Returns conversation metadata (id, name, source, timestamps,
linked workflow ids). Use ``agent_conversation_get`` to load
the full message history for a single conversation, or pass
the conversation id back to ``agent_chat`` to resume it.

source.description: Filter by origin: 'api' for conversations started via the MCP/API, 'web' for the Roboflow UI. Omit for all.

workflow_url.description: Filter to conversations linked to this workflow URL slug.

tools.name: agent_conversation_get
tools.title: Get Agent Conversation
tools.description:
Get a single agent conversation with its message history.

Returns the conversation metadata and the ordered list of the most
recent ``message_limit`` messages (role + text parts), plus
``total_messages`` with the full history size. Pass the same
``conversation_id`` back to ``agent_chat`` to continue the
conversation.

conversation_id.description: Conversation ID returned by agent_chat or agent_conversations_list.

message_limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return, counted from the most recent.

tools.name: agent_workflow_publish
tools.title: Publish Agent Workflow Draft
tools.description:
Publish the latest agent-edited draft of a workflow.

The agent never publishes on its own — every workflow it
creates or edits is saved as a draft. This tool promotes the
latest draft to a published version so it goes live for
callers using the workflow by id (``workflows_run``).

Errors with 400 if there is no draft to publish (i.e. the
published version already matches the latest draft).

Returns ``{ workflowId, workflowUrl, versionId, status }``.

workflow_url.description: URL slug of the workflow to publish (the 'url' field returned by agent_chat).

tools.name: projects_list
tools.title: List Projects
tools.description:
List projects in the workspace associated with the credential.

Returns ``{ projects, total, limit, offset }`` where ``projects``
holds up to ``limit`` entries (id, name, type, image count, and more)
and ``total`` is the full workspace project count. Page with
``offset`` when ``total`` exceeds ``limit``.

limit.description: Maximum number of projects to return

offset.description: Number of projects to skip, for paging

tools.name: projects_create
tools.title: Create Project
tools.description:
Create a new computer vision project.

Returns the created project's id, name, type, and url.

annotation.description: What you're annotating, as a dash-separated slug of letters, numbers, and dashes (e.g. 'defects', 'hard-hats').

license.description: Project license. Free public/research workspaces can only create public projects, so they must pick a non-Private license. Ask the user before choosing one on their behalf.

business_context.description: Brief description of the business problem this project addresses, if the user has shared one.

tools.name: projects_health
tools.title: Get Project Health
tools.description:
Get dataset health check for a project.

Running this for the first time or with regenerate=True might take up to a couple minutes.

Returns class balance, image quality issues, annotation statistics, and other dataset health metrics.

regenerate.description: Set to true to regenerate the health report from scratch.

tools.name: projects_get
tools.title: Get Project
tools.description:
Get detailed info about a project including versions, classes, splits, and trained models.

Returns full project details with workspace, project info, versions, and classes.

tools.name: projects_delete
tools.title: Delete Project
tools.description:
Delete a project, moving it to the workspace Trash.

This is a soft delete: the project (including its versions, images,
and models) stays in the Trash for 30 days and can be restored with
``trash_restore_project`` using the project's document id from the
delete response or ``trash_list``. After 30 days it is permanently
removed. Active trainings on the project are cancelled.

tools.name: projects_fork
tools.title: Fork Universe Project
tools.description:
Enqueue an async fork of a public Universe project into your workspace.

Provide either a Universe `url` or `source_project`.
Returns the platform's 202 payload verbatim — at minimum
`{ taskId, url }`, where `url` points at the async-task polling
endpoint. Poll completion with `async_tasks_get(task_id=taskId)`
every 5 seconds until `status` is terminal (`completed` or `failed`).
Processing may take up to 30 seconds to start.

source_project.description: Universe project slug to fork into your workspace; optional if url is provided

tools.name: datasets_rebalance_splits
tools.title: Rebalance Dataset Splits
tools.description:
Enqueue an async rebalance of a project's train/valid/test splits.

Use this to fix a starved or empty split — an empty test split blocks
training, and this is the only way to move images between splits after
upload.

`train`, `valid` and `test` are relative weights, not percentages: they
do not have to sum to 100, and each must be a whole number (70, not
70.5). `mode="rebalance"` moves the fewest images needed to reach the
ratios; `mode="shuffle"` reassigns every image.

Returns the platform's 202 payload verbatim — at minimum
`{ taskId, url }`, where `url` points at the async-task polling
endpoint. Poll completion with `async_tasks_get(task_id=taskId)`
every 5 seconds until `status` is terminal (`completed` or `failed`).

train.description: Target weight for the train split

valid.description: Target weight for the valid split

test.description: Target weight for the test split

mode.description: 'rebalance' moves the fewest images needed to hit the target ratios, leaving every other image where it is. 'shuffle' ignores current assignments and reassigns every image at random to match the ratios.

Learning before a custom model has been trained. Also use it for

tools.name: project_deployment_list_review_queues
tools.title: List Project Deployment Review Queues

tools.name: image_upload
tools.title: Upload Images
tools.description:
Upload local image files to a project via a zip.

Use this to ingest images that live on the user's machine: it zips the
local files and uploads them. To instead mirror images from a cloud
storage bucket (S3/GCS), use the datasource tools, not this one.

Returns a signed upload URL and step-by-step instructions; the upload itself
completes client-side. The MCP server never receives file bytes.

Requires the project slug and the image paths on the user's machine (plus
optional split and tags).

Remaining steps after this returns (detailed in the response instructions):
1. Zip the image paths (even one file → zip). Paths inside the zip set splits:
   train/, valid/ and test/ folders override the split argument per image.
2. HTTP PUT the zip to signedUrl.
3. Poll image_upload_status(task_id) every few seconds until completed or failed.

Images only — no annotation files in the zip. Use annotations_save to label later.
Pass add_to_dataset=true there to also add the image to the Dataset, which is what
makes it usable for training.
Up to 2 GB / 10k files. Signed URL expires in 1 hour.

split.description: Fallback split, used only for images whose path inside the zip has no split folder. Folders named train/valid/test in the zip override this per image.

batch_name.description: Group uploads under a named batch and annotation job

tag_names.description: Tags to attach to every uploaded image

business_context.description: Brief description of the business problem this upload addresses, if the user has shared one.

tools.name: image_upload_status
tools.title: Get Image Upload Status
tools.description:
Check the status of an image zip upload task.

Use after the zip has been PUT to the signed URL (image_upload step 2).
Poll every 3–5 seconds until status is completed or failed.

Returns status, progress while running, and result when terminal.

tools.name: images_update_metadata
tools.title: Update Image Metadata
tools.description:
Update metadata and tags on a single image. Metadata and tags can be useful to find images later in the platform.
Common metadata include photo location, camera, date.

Provide at least one of: metadata, remove_metadata, add_tags, remove_tags.
The same key cannot appear in both metadata and remove_metadata;
the same tag cannot appear in both add_tags and remove_tags.

Returns { success: true } on success.

metadata.description: Key-value pairs to set on user_metadata (values can be strings, numbers, or booleans)

add_tags.description: Tags to add (alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores; max 64 chars each)

tools.name: images_batch_update_metadata
tools.title: Batch Update Image Metadata
tools.description:
Batch-update metadata and tags on multiple images (async).

Each item in updates must contain an 'imageId' and at least one
mutation bucket. Same conflict rules as the single-image endpoint.

Returns { taskId, url } with status 202. Poll completion via
async_tasks_get with the returned taskId.

updates.description: List of update objects, each with 'imageId' (required) and at least one of: 'metadata', 'removeMetadata', 'addTags', 'removeTags'. Max 1000 items.

tools.name: images_workspace_search
tools.title: Search Workspace Images
tools.description:
Search images across the entire workspace using RoboQL.

The workspace is determined automatically from the API key —
no workspace or project parameter is needed. Just provide a query.

Use RoboQL syntax to filter by project, tag, metadata, and more.
Request the `url` field when you need a direct image URL.
Returns results with a continuationToken for pagination.

page_size.description: Maximum number of results per page

continuation_token.description: Token from a previous response to fetch the next page

fields.description: Fields to include per result (e.g. 'filename', 'url', 'owner', 'projects', 'split', 'annotations', 'tags', 'user_metadata'). Include 'url' to access the image directly.

tools.name: images_search
tools.title: Search Project Images
tools.description: Search for images inside a project.

query.description: Search prompt for project-scoped image discovery

limit.description: Maximum number of results

like_image.description: Find images visually similar to this image id/name

in_dataset.description: Filter to images currently in the dataset

batch.description: Filter to images in any batch

batch_id.description: Filter to a specific batch id

annotation_job.description: Filter to images assigned to any annotation job

annotation_job_id.description: Filter to a specific annotation job id

fields.description: Fields to include in each result. Include 'url' to access the image directly.

tools.name: universe_dataset_images_search
tools.title: Search Universe Dataset Images
tools.description:
Search images inside a public Universe dataset given its URL.

Accepts a full Universe dataset URL and derives the workspace and
project slugs from it before searching the dataset's images.

query.description: Search prompt for image discovery inside this public dataset

limit.description: Maximum number of results

tools.name: media_analyze
tools.title: Analyze Image or Video
tools.description:
Analyze an image or short video with a vision model to understand its contents.

Returns a structured analysis: a summary, the distinct objects present with
approximate counts, the best-fitting CV task (detection, segmentation,
classification, OCR, tracking...), candidate class names, whether those classes
fall within the 80 COCO classes (drives model-family selection), motion notes
for video, and workflow recommendations.

Pass any public HTTPS URL directly — image results from images_search,
images_workspace_search, or universe_dataset_images_search already include a
usable `url` field. For a local file on the user's machine, call media_upload
first and analyze the URL it produces.

This is a stateless one-shot primitive: nothing is recorded in a conversation.
For multi-turn analysis tied to workspace context (or when the user should see
the exchange in their Solutions chat history), prefer agent_chat and reference
the media URL in the message.

Costs workspace credits (one vision-model call per invocation). Storage allows
videos up to 100 MB, but ANALYSIS is capped at ~15 MB by the vision gateway's
url fetcher; trim longer footage before analyzing.

url.description: Public HTTPS URL of the image or video to analyze.

media_type.description: Kind of media at the URL.

question.description: Optional focus question, phrased in the context of the user's goal.

tools.name: media_upload
tools.title: Upload Media for Analysis
tools.description:
Prepare a local image or video for analysis with media_analyze.

Returns a short-lived signed upload URL plus step-by-step instructions; the
upload itself completes client-side (the MCP server never receives file bytes).
After the PUT, call media_upload_finalize to validate the bytes. For images and
small videos it returns a durable `url` to pass straight to media_analyze; for
videos over the analysis budget it returns `needsTrim: true` with a
`videoAssetId`, and you call media_trim to get the analyzable clip url.

Only needed for files on the user's machine; media already reachable by an
HTTPS URL (including Roboflow-hosted images) can go straight to media_analyze.

Finalized images and videos are saved into the workspace Asset Library
(reusable across the workspace; re-uploading identical bytes reuses the
existing asset instead of duplicating it). The analyzable copy ends up on a
public CDN at an unguessable URL.

filename.description: Filename of the local file, e.g. 'floor.jpg'.

tools.name: media_trim
tools.title: Trim Video for Analysis
tools.description:
Cut a clip from an Asset Library video and get an analyzable public url.

Use after media_upload_finalize returns `needsTrim: true`. The simplest call is
media_trim(video_asset_id) with no window: the server cuts the longest clip the
~15 MB analysis budget allows from the start (typically up to ~95 seconds; often
the entire video, since long windows are re-encoded, downscaled to at most
1280px, to fit). Pass start_seconds/duration_seconds only when your user cares
about a specific segment.

The response tells you exactly what happened: `clipSeconds` (what was actually
cut), `requestedSeconds`, `clamped: true` when the server shrank the window,
plus authoritative `videoDurationSeconds` and `maxClipSeconds` from the
server-side probe. Report the real clipSeconds to your user; to cover the rest
of a long video, cut the next clip at start_seconds + clipSeconds and repeat.

Only the published clip is re-encoded; the full-quality video stays untouched
in the Asset Library.

start_seconds.description: Where the clip starts, in seconds.

duration_seconds.description: Clip length in seconds. Omit to cut as much as fits the analysis budget from start_seconds (the server decides the maximal window).

tools.name: media_upload_finalize
tools.title: Finalize Media Upload
tools.description:
Validate a staged upload (from media_upload) and publish it.

Checks the uploaded bytes match the declared media type and size limits. Images
become workspace Asset Library assets (the response includes their `sourceId`)
and return a durable public `url` to pass to media_analyze.

Videos always become Asset Library records (`videoAssetId`). Small videos also
return a durable `url` right away (`needsTrim: false`). Videos over the analysis
budget return `needsTrim: true`: call media_trim(video_asset_id) with no window
to get the maximal analyzable clip, and read the authoritative numbers from its
response. If you passed duration_seconds here, the response also includes
`maxClipSeconds` and `wholeVideoFits` (true when one clip covers the entire
video, so there is nothing to ask the user). Ask YOUR USER which segment matters
only when the video is longer than one clip can cover. The full video stays in
the Asset Library either way.

The staged object is removed whether validation passes or fails, so a failed
finalize means starting over with a fresh media_upload.

media_type.description: Kind of file that was uploaded.

duration_seconds.description: Video duration in seconds, if known (e.g. from ffprobe on the local file). Enables the maxClipSeconds hint in the response for oversized videos.

tools.name: annotations_save
tools.title: Save Annotations
tools.description:
Save an annotation for an existing image.

By default this only stores the annotation: it does not change whether the
image belongs to the project Dataset. Pass add_to_dataset=true to also add
the image to the Dataset. That membership is what makes the image count
toward a dataset version, so an image that is uploaded and annotated but
never added to the Dataset will show up as 0 images in versions_generate.

Set prediction_routing to ``review`` to request an automatic move from the
target-project batch into a Review job only when the image has
target-project batch membership and no target-project annotation-job
membership. Set it to ``unassigned`` to suppress that move and preserve
existing batch, annotation-job, and Dataset memberships. Prediction
uploads never add Dataset membership, even when add_to_dataset is true,
and existing Dataset membership is preserved. Neither value guarantees
movement to a named queue.

Saving onto an image that already has annotations fails with a 409
conflict unless you pass overwrite=true, which replaces the existing
annotation. Classification projects never hit that conflict: their
saves already overwrite.

image_id.description: ID of the image to annotate

annotation_content.description: The annotation content (XML, JSON, or text)

labelmap.description: Label map for Darknet/TXT annotations, e.g. {'0': 'cat', '1': 'dog'}

add_to_dataset.description: Also add the image to the project Dataset for training. Prediction uploads never add Dataset membership, but preserve existing Dataset membership.

prediction_routing.description: Treat the upload as a prediction. 'review' requests an automatic move from the target-project batch into a Review job only when the image has target-project batch membership and no target-project annotation-job membership. 'unassigned' suppresses that move and preserves existing batch, annotation-job, and Dataset memberships. Prediction uploads never add Dataset membership, and existing Dataset membership is preserved. Neither value guarantees movement to a named queue.

overwrite.description: Replace the existing annotation on this image instead of failing. Saving onto an image that already has annotations returns a 409 conflict unless this is true. Classification projects are exempt: their saves always overwrite, so the conflict cannot happen there.

tools.name: autolabel_models_list
tools.title: List Auto-Label Models
tools.description:
List the foundation models available for hosted auto-labeling in this workspace.

Returns ``{models: [...]}``. Each entry's ``id`` (e.g. ``sam3-rle``,
``gemini-boxes``) is a valid ``model`` value for ``autolabel_start``
with ``model_type='foundational'``. Entries carry ``guidance`` on when
to prefer each model, ``projectTypes`` / ``excludedProjectTypes`` they
support, ``ontologyFormat`` (``promptMap``: prompts are sent to the
model; ``classes``: only class names are used), ``creditsPerImage``,
and ``available`` with an ``unavailableReason`` when the workspace's
plan blocks a model. Call this before ``autolabel_start`` to pick a
model instead of assuming which ones exist. When the user has not
chosen a model, follow up with ``autolabel_preview`` to compare the
candidates on one sample image before committing to a job.

tools.name: autolabel_preview
tools.title: Preview Auto-Label Model
tools.description:
Preview one image with a foundation model to judge it before starting an auto-label job.

Use this as the model-selection loop when the user has not picked a model:
1. Call autolabel_models_list and order the candidates (the default first,
   then whatever the guidance recommends for the ontology at hand).
2. Pick one representative image from the batch (e.g. from the batch or
   image listing tools) and preview it with the first candidate.
3. Judge the summary: entries in classesWithNoDetections, a suspiciously
   low totalDetections, or blockErrors mean the model likely will not
   label this data well. Preview the next candidate and compare.
4. Start the real job with the winner via autolabel_start, using the same
   ontology.

Previews are free: no job is created and no credits are spent. Returns
``{model, summary, predictions, blockErrors?}``; summary.byClass carries
per-class counts and max confidence, and predictions are trimmed to
class, confidence, and box geometry (polygon and mask geometry is
dropped to keep responses small).

image.description: Sample image as an HTTPS URL or base64-encoded string.

ontology.description: Classes to detect: either {'class name': 'text prompt'} or a plain list of class names. When omitted, the dataset's own classes are used.

confidence_threshold.description: Detection threshold between 0.0 and 1.0 (sam3 only; gemini reports fixed confidence).

tools.name: autolabel_start
tools.title: Start Auto-Label Job
tools.description:
Start a hosted auto-label job over a batch of images.

Call ``autolabel_models_list`` first to pick a foundation model; its
entry ids (e.g. 'gemini-boxes' for open-vocabulary object detection)
are valid ``model`` values. If the user has not chosen a model, run
``autolabel_preview`` on a sample image per candidate and start the
job with the best one. Returns ``{jobId, annotationJobId, message}``.
Poll progress with ``autolabel_job_get`` using the returned ``jobId``.

batch_id.description: Source batch ID containing images to auto-label

model.description: Model identifier. For model_type='foundational', a model id from autolabel_models_list (e.g. 'sam3-rle', 'sam3-polygon', 'gemini-boxes'; the bare 'sam3' also works). For model_type='roboflow', a Roboflow model id like 'project-slug/version' or 'workspace-slug/model-id'.

model_type.description: How to interpret `model`. 'foundational' uses a hosted foundation model (sent as-is; the backend resolves catalog ids like 'gemini-boxes' to their execution path). 'roboflow' uses a Roboflow-trained model and is sent as 'custom_roboflow' with the id passed in modelOptions.modelId.

ontology.description: Mapping of class name -> text prompt used to label, e.g. {'cat': 'a cat', 'dog': 'a dog'}. tools.name: versions_get

Get info about a dataset version including splits and its trainings.

Readiness fields report generation state for callers that need to poll:
``generating`` is true only while generation looks actively in progress,
and ``ready`` is true once generation is not active AND at least one
train/valid/test split count is present. Generation usually takes several
minutes and can take up to about an hour on large datasets, with
``progress`` stuck at 0 or null for most of that wait: that is normal,
not stuck. Poll this tool roughly once a minute until ``ready`` is true.
Trainability floors (min images per split, labels, NAS mins) are enforced
by the platform train endpoint; if ``ready`` is false only because splits
are empty/insufficient, waiting will not help. Call trainings_create and
surface that error.

tools.name: models_list
tools.title: List Models
tools.description:
List trained models associated with a project.

Returns ``{models, total, returned, limit, offset, truncated}``. Each row
carries `metrics`, and (for NAS children) `nasFamily` and `group`, plus
a derived `recommended` flag when the model is the recommended pick for
any (metric, hardware) bucket on its parent version.

`metrics` is sparse and its keys depend on the run. An ordinary training
carries accuracy only, e.g. {map50, precision, recall, f1}. `latency`
and `paretoOptimalFor` come from NAS mining, so they appear on NAS
children and not on ordinary trainings; `metrics` may also be null.
Do not assume a key is present - read what is there.

Two shapes of NAS child are in the data. Newer runs report
`latency` as a map keyed by target hardware (e.g. {"AI1": 6.69,
"T4": 1.98}) and `paretoOptimalFor` entries as "<hardware>:<metric>"
(e.g. "T4:map_50_95"). Older runs report a scalar `latency` with a
sibling `metrics.hardware` (e.g. "gpu") and bare-metric
`paretoOptimalFor` entries (e.g. "map_50"). Branch on the type of
`latency` rather than indexing it. `recommended` is the flattened union of the platform's
per-hardware winners, so more than one row in a group carries it and it
cannot tell you which hardware a child won; `paretoOptimalFor` is
frontier membership, not the recommendation. The authoritative map,
`recommendedByHardware`, exists only on legacy version-based summaries
and is absent from modern MMPV runs. NAS children with
`nasFamily: "baseline"` are stock RF-DETR models trained on the same
data; they carry no `paretoOptimalFor` and are never `recommended`.

A project with NAS runs can have hundreds of models, so the result is
always bounded: filter with `version_number` and/or `group=<modelGroup>`
(the canonical "list NAS models per run" path), and page with
`limit`/`offset`. `truncated` is true when more rows remain past the page.

group.description: Optional NAS modelGroup to scope the list to a single NAS run. Get this value from trainings_list, which returns it without the child list that trainings_get inlines.

version_number.description: Filter to a single version's models. Strongly recommended on projects with NAS runs, which can have hundreds of models across versions.

limit.description: Maximum number of models to return (default 50, max 200).

offset.description: Offset into the (filtered) result set, for paging.

use workflow_specs_run with a visualization block instead.

tools.name: trainings_describe_recipe
tools.title: Describe Train Recipe
tools.description:
Describe the tuning surface for a model type and get a ready-to-submit train recipe.

Returns two things:

- ``schema``: the valid tuning knobs for this model on this version,
  namely manifest hyperparameters with hard bounds (``valid``) and
  advisory ranges (``advice.low``/``advice.high``) for a deliberate,
  hypothesis-driven change. A descriptor's ``advice.default`` is the
  tuned value the server applies when you omit the key, so a sparse
  recipe is the good default; a descriptor with NO ``advice.default``
  is one only the trainer can resolve (it derives the value from the
  dataset at train time), so leave those out unless you specifically
  intend to override the derivation. Also included: the task-supported
  online augmentation steps with their field contracts, the supported
  online preprocessing steps, and input/resolution rules.
- ``template``: a ready-to-submit ``trainRecipe`` for this model type.
  Edit the knobs you want to change, then pass the whole dict as
  ``train_recipe`` to trainings_create.

An unknown ``model_type`` fails with a 404 whose error body lists the
valid model types for the project's task.

version_number.description: Version number the training will run on.

model_type.description: Model architecture ID to describe, e.g. 'rfdetr-medium'. If an invalid ID is passed, the 404 error lists the valid model types for the project's task.

tools.name: trainings_create
tools.title: Create Training
tools.description:
Create a training on a dataset version.

IMPORTANT: A dataset version must exist before training. Use the
versions_generate tool first to create one with the desired
preprocessing and augmentation settings.

A modern (MMPV) version may own MANY trainings — concurrent and
repeated runs are allowed. Legacy single-model-per-version (SMPV)
versions already hold their one model and reject a second training with
a 409; generate a fresh version to train more models. To inspect a
version's trainings, use trainings_list; to monitor a specific run, use
trainings_get with the returned training_id.

MODEL CHOICE: for object detection and instance segmentation, prefer a
NAS parent over a single named architecture: searching the architecture
space against this dataset usually beats hand-tuning one. See the
model_type description for ids and prerequisites.

To customize hyperparameters or online augmentation, call
trainings_describe_recipe FIRST, edit its ``template`` (set
``template["hyperparameters"]``; add augmentation steps as
``{name, params: {...}}`` dicts), and pass the whole dict as
train_recipe. Recipe hyperparameters are sparse: keys you leave out
keep their server-side defaults, which are the tuned values, so omitting a
key is the right default, not a missed opportunity. Set a knob when you
have a specific reason to move it, not to explore. Recipe training
requires the workspace's online-augmentation training entitlement
(403 otherwise).

COMPARING ARCHITECTURES: launch one trainings_create per candidate
(MMPV versions allow many concurrent trainings) and keep each returned
trainingId. Include a NAS parent as one of the candidates whenever its
prerequisites are met, e.g. 'rfdetr-medium' vs 'yolo26m' vs
'rfdetr-nas-parent'.

A NAS arm returns a frontier of models rather than one. Resolve it with
trainings_list -> modelGroup -> models_list(group=<modelGroup>), whose
docstring describes the per-child fields; use trainings_list rather than
trainings_get, which inlines every child and defeats the paging. Which
child represents that arm depends on the question being asked, and the
obvious reading of the `recommended` flag is wrong - read the
training-and-evaluation skill before comparing arms or deploying.

This tool validates that the dataset version has finished generating and
that the required export is ready before starting. If either is not
ready the call fails with a 400 explaining what to poll and for how
long: version generation can take up to about an hour on large datasets
and reports 0 progress for most of it. Retry until it succeeds rather
than giving up after one attempt.

Training runs in the background on Roboflow servers.

model_type.description: Model architecture ID. For object detection and instance segmentation, prefer Neural Architecture Search: 'rfdetr-nas-parent' (detection) or 'rfdetr-nas-seg-parent' (instance segmentation). NAS searches the RF-DETR space against this dataset and returns a speed/accuracy frontier, so it is the option most likely to produce the best model for the user's data. Two prerequisites: >=15 validation images (check versions_get splits.valid before choosing) and a plan entitled to NAS. The entitlement is not readable from the MCP, so it surfaces as a rejection from this tool with code 'nas_not_available_for_plan'. Treat that as a plan limit rather than a transient error, do not retry it, and fall back to a named model below. The remedy depends on the plan carried on that error: self-serve plans upgrade, enterprise/legacy need NAS enabled on the workspace, so say NAS is unavailable on the current plan and may need an upgrade or workspace enablement rather than naming one. Named models: 'rfdetr-medium' (detection), 'rfdetr-seg-medium' (instance segmentation), 'yolov11n' (fast YOLO), 'yolo26n-pose' (keypoint), 'vit-base-patch16-224-in21k' (classification), 'qwen3_5-2b-peft' (multimodal/VLM). Keypoint, classification, semantic segmentation and VLM tasks have no NAS option. If an invalid ID is passed, the API returns the full list of valid model types for the project's task. Read the training-and-evaluation skill for the complete list and model selection guidance.

speed.description: Training speed (deprecated — model_type is usually sufficient)

checkpoint.description: Checkpoint to initialize from (COCO, a Universe model, or a previous version)

epochs.description: Number of training epochs. With a train_recipe this folds into the recipe's hyperparameters (a value set inside the recipe wins) and has no fixed cap; trainings_describe_recipe reports the recommended range per model type (the epochs descriptor's advice.low/high). Without a recipe, the server caps this value at 300.

train_recipe.description: Full trainRecipe dict, together with the model_type it was minted for (model_type is required with it). Get one from trainings_describe_recipe: take its `template`, set template['hyperparameters'] (sparse; omitted keys keep server-side defaults), add augmentation steps as {name, params: {...}} dicts, and pass the whole dict here. If the recipe's hyperparameters omit epochs, the epochs param is folded in; an epochs set inside the recipe wins.

business_context.description: Brief description of the business problem this model addresses, if the user has shared one.

tools.name: models_upload_custom_weights
tools.title: Custom Weights Upload Guide
tools.description:
Get the recipe for uploading locally trained model weights to Roboflow.

This tool never uploads anything. Weights packaging must run on the
machine that has the checkpoint (it reads the weights file and needs
torch), and this MCP server cannot read the user's filesystem. Calling
it returns the client-side recipe: how to run the upload with the
Roboflow Python SDK on the machine where the weights live. Pass
whatever arguments you already know; the response names the matching
upload mode and echoes them back for the SDK call. Do not infer the
target project, version, or model name from the checkpoint; those come
from the user.

model_type.description: Custom model type you plan to upload, e.g. 'yolov8n', 'yolov11s', 'rfdetr-base', 'yolonas', or a supported PaliGemma/Florence type. Optional.

model_path.description: Directory containing the trained model artifacts on the machine where training ran. Optional.

version_number.description: Dataset version for a versioned deploy. Omit for a workspace model upload.

model_name.description: Model name for a workspace upload. Ask the user for it; never invent one.

tools.name: trainings_list
tools.title: List Trainings
tools.description:
List the trainings on a dataset version.

A version may own many trainings. Returns one entry per run:
``{ trainingId, status, createdAt, modelType, modelGroup, modelIds }``.
``createdAt`` is when the run was launched (ISO 8601 UTC), or null if
unknown. Entries are sorted oldest-to-newest by ``createdAt``. Statuses
are surfaced verbatim (e.g. 'finished', 'failed', 'cancelled',
'stopped', 'running'). Pick a ``trainingId`` and pass it to
trainings_get, trainings_cancel, or trainings_stop.

version_number.description: Version number whose trainings to list.

tools.name: trainings_get
tools.title: Get Training
tools.description:
Get a training's status, produced models, and metrics.

With ``training_id``, returns that run:
``{ trainingId, status, createdAt, modelType, modelGroup, modelCount,
    models: [ { modelId, nasFamily, metrics, recommended }, ... ],
    recommendedByHardware?, mining? }``. ``createdAt`` is when the run
was launched (ISO 8601 UTC), or null if unknown. Statuses are surfaced
verbatim — 'failed', 'cancelled', and 'stopped' are distinct.

Without ``training_id``: returns the version's sole run, or all runs
when a version owns several trainings. Multi-run responses are sorted
oldest-to-newest by launch time.

For headline metrics (mAP/precision/recall) on a specific model, use
model_evals_list to find the version's evaluations and then
model_evals_get and its siblings. Those tools require the
``model-eval:read`` scope, so eval lookup is deliberately kept out of
this tool — monitoring a run only needs ``version:read``.

For full per-model metadata on a NAS run, call models_list with the
returned modelGroup.

version_number.description: Version number whose training to summarize.

training_id.description: Training id from trainings_list. Omit to summarize the version's sole run; required when the version owns several runs.

tools.name: trainings_cancel
tools.title: Cancel Training
tools.description:
Cancel an in-flight training run.

Works for any architecture. For NAS runs the underlying handler
accepts the ``mining`` status — same call cancels mining or training
phases.

version_number.description: Version number whose training to cancel.

training_id.description: Training id from trainings_list to cancel a specific run. Omit to target the version's sole run; required when the version owns several runs.

continue_if_no_refund.description: If true, cancel even when the run is past the refund window. Default false (the server will return refund:false without cancelling).

tools.name: trainings_stop
tools.title: Stop Training
tools.description:
Request an early stop on an in-flight training run.

Distinct from cancel: the run finishes the current phase gracefully
(mining or training) instead of terminating immediately.

version_number.description: Version number whose training to stop early.

training_id.description: Training id from trainings_list to stop a specific run. Omit to target the version's sole run; required when the version owns several runs.

tools.name: trainings_delete
tools.title: Delete Training
tools.description:
Delete a training run, moving it to the workspace Trash.

This is a soft delete: the training stays in the Trash for 30 days
and can be restored with ``trash_restore_training`` using the
training id. After 30 days it is permanently removed. Deleting may
repoint or remove the ``{project}/{version}`` serving alias; the
response reports the alias action taken.

version_number.description: Version number that owns the training run.

training_id.description: Training id from trainings_list identifying the run to delete.

tools.name: models_star_nas
tools.title: Star NAS Model
tools.description:
Star or unstar a NAS-trained model.

NAS-only by design — the server rejects non-NAS modelTypes with a
``MODEL_NOT_NAS`` error. Starring triggers TRT compilation for the
model's recommended hardware so the model becomes deployable as an
edge target.

model_id.description: Public model id (the `url` field from models_list[] or models[].modelId from trainings_get), e.g. 'beer-can-hackathon-410-nas-gpu-b'. Just the bare id — workspace prefix added automatically.

starred.description: True to star, false to unstar.

tools.name: model_evals_list
tools.title: List Model Evaluations
tools.description:
List model evaluations in the current workspace.

Returns ``{evals: [...]}`` where each entry has evalId, status,
project (URL slug), versionId, modelId, modelUrl, and createdAt. Use
``model_evals_get`` for the headline ``summary`` (mAP/precision/recall)
on a specific eval.

Two model identifiers are returned and they are NOT interchangeable:
``modelId`` is the eval's internal id (the ``model_id`` filter key here);
``modelUrl`` is the resolvable public id that ``models_get`` / ``models_infer``
accept and that joins to ``models_list[].url`` and ``trainings_get`` results.

At most one of ``project_id`` / ``version_number`` / ``model_id`` may be
set per call (most-specific wins). Combinations return 400.

tools.name: model_evals_get
tools.title: Get Model Evaluation
tools.description:
Get the top-level summary for a single model evaluation.

Returns the eval metadata plus a ``summary`` of mAP / precision /
recall on done evals, and an ``app_url`` deep link into the UI panel.

The ``modelUrl`` field is the resolvable public model id (feed it to
``models_get`` / ``models_infer``); ``modelId`` is the eval's internal id.

Get per-split mAP results for an eval.

Returns ``{splits: {train, valid, test}}`` where each split has

(small/medium/large), and ``perClass`` breakdowns.

tools.name: model_evals_get_confidence_sweep

Get the precision/recall/F1 confidence sweep for an eval.

For each split returns ``perThreshold`` (metrics keyed by threshold

and ``perClass`` sweeps.

tools.name: model_evals_get_performance_by_class

Returns ``{split, classes: [{className, map50, map50_95, map75,
precision, recall, f1, optimalThreshold}, ...]}``.

tools.name: model_evals_get_confusion_matrix

Get the confusion matrix for an eval.

Returns ``{split, confidenceThreshold, classes, matrix}`` where

Returns ``{clustering, preprocessing, clusters: [...]}`` — useful

Returns ``{split, confidenceThreshold, totalImages, offset, limit,

tools.name: model_evals_get_recommendations

tools.name: workflows_list
